what_happened.line: Town Meeting approved buying the Saliba land for conservation and recreation, with borrowing authorized and state grants offsetting most of it.
Members defeated the proposed replacement earth removal and fill bylaw after four amendments had passed.
Members added 189 Cross Road to the sewer service area as originally written, after an amendment limiting the extension failed.
The police contract article was passed over because no appropriation was needed for the first year of the contract.
A non-binding vote favored demolishing the old primary school; members also accepted Butterfly Lane as a public way.

why_it_matters: The Saliba purchase adds land debt payments to the maturing debt line, which the town manager said fits within policy limits without an override.
Accepting Butterfly Lane moves road maintenance onto the town budget, mostly taxes, and the earth removal bylaw's defeat leaves the existing rules in place.
The primary school vote is advisory only, so any demolition spending would still need a later vote.

what_happened.line: Town Meeting defeated Article 42, which would have moved solar special permits from the Planning Board to the Zoning Board of Appeals, on a counted vote.
A rezoning of Shirley Road parcels to the office park industrial district passed unanimously, with more than the two-thirds needed.
The Historical Society's School Street easement (citizen petition Article 39) was amended and then approved.
Articles 40 and 41 were passed over so a charrette and neighbor meetings could be arranged.
Article 43 was passed over by voice vote, and the meeting closed.

why_it_matters: Solar special permits stay with the Planning Board, so the same board will keep reviewing solar projects and their buffer requirements.
The Shirley Road rezoning changes what can be built on those parcels, and the School Street easement gives the Historical Society a right over town-adjacent land.
watch_next: The charrette and neighbor meetings promised for the land in Articles 40 and 41, which may return at a later Town Meeting.

what_happened.line: Article 21, letting selectmen convey the old primary school by lease or sale, failed on a hand count and again on a recount, short of the two-thirds needed.
An amendment to change "convey" to transfer or lease only was defeated, and debate on article 21 was ended by vote after long discussion.
Town Meeting passed the 2% COLA salary plan for non-union staff and transfers to the stabilization funds and the OPEB trust, all unanimously.
Sewer, solid waste, water, PEG access and cemetery articles passed unanimously; article 18 was passed over.
Article 22 on the Brooks house was under discussion when the captions end; the moderator said the meeting would push on rather than recess to Monday.

why_it_matters: The old primary school stays under the current approval rules: selectmen cannot lease or sell it without a new Town Meeting vote, and its upkeep stays on the town budget, mostly taxes.
The savings transfers and the 2% COLA were set at this meeting, so they shape future capital funding and the town's payroll costs.
Enterprise funds for sewer, solid waste and water are paid by user fees, and the sewer budget was described as having no rate increases.
watch_next: The outcome of article 22 on the Brooks house, which was still under discussion when the captions end.
Whether article 21 or a revised version of it comes back at a later Town Meeting.
